content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — § 21.1 cap basis is illusory.**

The liability architecture is otherwise strong: the cap is expressly mutual, § 21.2 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully treats data-restoration, replacement-services, notice and incident-response costs as direct), and § 21.3 delivers the full preferred carve-out set plus confirmation that Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not "damages".

The problem is the measure: "Fees" is defined in § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee, which § 1.6 fixes as a one-time USD 12,000 charge under the first Order Form. So the "twelve months' fees" cap is in substance a USD 12,000 cap that ignores every subsequent Order Form — well below the fallback of 12 months' fees and within walk-away territory.

Redline (validated, ok:true) makes the smallest possible edit to § 21.1, replacing the defined-term basis with the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000, leaving mutuality and the Excluded Claims carve-outs untouched.
